ai.title: Add PostHog env vars to .env.example
ai.summary: Added NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_API_KEY and NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST_URL to .env.example. These variables configure client-side PostHog analytics. The change also fixes the missing newline at the end of the file.

eli5.text: The project added two new configuration entries to its example settings file, so developers setting up the software on their own computers can now paste in the credentials and server address for the analytics tool they use to track how people use the app. The change also fixed a small formatting glitch where the last line of the file was missing its ending line break, which some tools expect for clean file handling.

entries.title: Quiet the console.error when loading node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch

ai.title: Suppress node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch console.error on load
ai.summary: Temporarily stubs console.error around require('@homebridge/node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch') in npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts. Prevents noisy stderr output when optional native bindings fail to load. Scoped to CLI tool handlers. Restores original console.error immediately after require.

eli5.text: When the assistant starts certain command-line tools, a part of the software that manages terminal windows sometimes prints error-like messages to the screen, even though nothing actually went wrong. The change quietly hides those messages so your terminal stays clean. If you run a CLI tool that uses this assistant feature, you will no longer see unexpected red error text appear while it loads. The fix is already live in the CLI tool handlers.

ai.title: Rename Oliver case study file to oliver-lukesch.mdx
ai.summary: Renamed `web/src/content/case-studies/oliver.mdx` to `oliver-lukesch.mdx` for consistent naming. Updated content to explicitly name the company `StartMatch` with a link. Internal content structure change.

eli5.text: The case study about Oliver Lukesch now clearly names the company he runs as StartMatch, with a link to its website, wherever visitors read his story on the company's site. Previously, the section only described what his company does without naming it or linking to it directly. The underlying file that stores this story was also given a more descriptive name that includes his last name, so the team can find it more easily when working behind the scenes.

ai.title: UsageLimits enum to const object; capitalize lowercases
ai.summary: UsageLimits in common/src/constants.ts converted from TS enum to as-const object plus derived type. capitalize in common/src/util/string.ts now lowercases remaining characters. Covers shared core constants and string utils. Breaks enum reverse-mapping assumptions if relied upon.

eli5.text: When the app capitalizes something like a sentence or a label, it now forces the rest of the letters to lowercase, so mixed-case text like 'iPhone' becomes 'IPhone'. The internal list that defines different user plans and their limits (like who counts as anonymous, free, or paid) was reorganized from a numbered-style list into a plain labeled list, which is mostly invisible but could affect any tools that relied on the old numbering behavior to look things up. This is live now and part of the shared code that powers the app.

ai.title: tool-handlers: hoist pty console.error suppression, shorten German
ai.summary: console.error suppression for pty require moved out of try block into module scope with finally restore. isNotACommand German string check shortened from full phrase to 'konnte nicht gefunden werden'. Internal refactor only in npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the app was reorganized so that a temporary fix for suppressing noisy error messages is now set up before any code tries to load, rather than inside a section that could fail. This means errors that used to pop up when loading certain tools are less likely to interrupt the process. Additionally, the wording used to detect when something is not a valid command was simplified to a shorter phrase, making it easier to match common error messages. These changes are internal and improve stability without altering visible features.

ai.title: Switch o1-preview to o1, add reasoning handling
ai.summary: Model constant `o1` updated from `o1-preview` to `o1` in `common/src/constants.ts`. `backend/src/openai-api.ts` implements specific non-streaming handling for o-series models with `reasoning_effort: 'high'` and Zod validation. `backend/src/planning.ts` switches from `promptOpenAIStream` to `promptOpenAI` for planning tasks. OpenAI SDK dependency bumped to `^4.78.1`.

eli5.text: The software now uses OpenAI's newer o1 model (instead of the older o1-preview) for complex planning tasks, and it asks that model to think harder before responding. When you request a multi-step plan, you'll experience slightly longer wait times because the system now uses a non-streaming call with high reasoning effort rather than a fast, partial-response stream. The developer tools were also updated so that this behavior only kicks in for o-series models, while other models keep their original speed.

ai.title: hasLazyEdit lowercases content before matching
ai.summary: hasLazyEdit in common/src/util/string.ts now applies toLowerCase().trim() to input before running detection checks. This fixes case-sensitive misses where lazy edit markers like '// REST OF THE' or uppercase comment variants failed to trigger the checker. The regex patterns and string literals remain unchanged, operating on the normalized cleanedContent.

eli5.text: The assistant now correctly spots edit hints in your code samples even when they use capital letters or extra spaces, so markers like "// REST OF THE" or "<!--...existing... -->" will reliably trigger the lazy edit mode. Previously, uppercase or oddly formatted hints were silently ignored, causing the assistant to miss your intent to leave parts of the code untouched. This fix is live today for all users of the assistant's code editing features.

ai.title: Move sleep util from helpers to promise
ai.summary: Relocated `sleep` helper from `common/util/helpers` to `common/util/promise`. Updated imports in backend (`claude.ts`, `generate-patch.ts`) and web components (`referrals`, `InteractiveTerminalDemo`, `sign-in-button`). Deleted `common/src/util/helpers.ts`.

eli5.text: The team moved a small utility called 'sleep', which makes the app pause for a moment between steps, into a different folder that already handles similar tasks. This doesn't change any visible behavior you'd notice, but it helps keep the code organized so future work is easier to maintain. Nothing you see or do in the app will feel different because of this change.

ai.title: Deepseek config adds 90s timeout and 3 retries
ai.summary: Backend `deepseek-api.ts` sets `timeout: 90_000` and `maxRetries: 3` on the OpenAI client initialization. Constants `DEEPSEEK_TIMEOUT_MS` and `DEEPSEEK_MAX_RETRIES` define these values. This applies to the singleton `deepseekClient` used across backend requests.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant a question that takes a while to answer, it will now wait up to 90 seconds before giving up instead of timing out sooner. If the request briefly fails, it will automatically try sending it again up to three times, so you are less likely to see an interruption caused by a temporary hiccup.
